title: Howler

scenario.title: Clean up a file or a pipe
scenario.body: A text tool is most useful in a pipeline: cat notes.txt | ./howler.py - -o loud.txt. The book reads a word or a file, but not a pipe. Files saved by Windows Notepad start with an invisible mark that shouldn't end up in the output, and a typo in the output folder shouldn't crash the program. Handle all three without breaking any of the author's tests.

character.name: Howie
character.role: a howler monkey who SHOUTS EVERYTHING

tagline: Howie is a howler monkey. Whatever you whisper, Howie SHOUTS. Howie can shout what you type, what you pour down the pipe, or shout it onto a scroll to keep.

brain_blurbs.real: Shouts words, files and pipes, and never trips over a bad folder.

rules.test_usage: Explains itself when you ask for help
rules.test_text_stdout: Shouts what you type: "foo bar baz" becomes "FOO BAR BAZ"
rules.test_text_outfile: Can shout onto a file instead of the screen
rules.test_file: Can shout a whole file (three poems) onto another file
rules.test_reads_a_pipe: A dash (-) means "shout whatever comes down the pipe"
rules.test_pipe_into_a_file: Can take from the pipe and shout onto a file
rules.test_notepad_mark_is_dropped: Ignores the invisible mark Windows Notepad hides at the start of files
rules.test_bad_output_folder_is_a_polite_error: A folder that doesn't exist gets a polite message, not a crash
rules.test_keeps_every_line: Empty lines in the middle stay put
rules.test_shouting_twice_changes_nothing: Shouting something already shouted changes nothing
